verdicts.strongest_argument: The filings are reachable and genuinely unaggregated, so this belongs in the 20-40 band, but it dies on size. Not one share count or dollar value appears anywhere in this capture for any of the three 144s or two Form 4s - no body is stored - and the company trades 66,237,575 shares a day on a $9.50bn market cap. For insider intents-to-sell to be informative against that, they would have to be a multiple of a day's volume, and typical executive plan sales at a company of this size are a rounding error on a single session. Three 144s inside seven days is also the signature of a scheduled window opening after a blackout, which at a name reporting in early September means the mid-August window - exactly where these sit. The finding's affirmative argument is the one I am instructed not to accept: 'if the market had priced insiders exiting into the rally, the run-in would not be +30%'. That is the run-up standing in for an option reading, and the hunter concedes half of it by noting the 30.1% and the volume figure come from the baseline tape rather than from any document. The retail stream's failure to mention insider selling is not evidence about the marginal price-setter in a stock with 66m shares of daily institutional turnover.

There is no bar in mid-August where the market can be seen absorbing an unusual seller - the rally is continuous through the filing dates. Median historical reaction is 5.9%, so this print's own expected move is an order of magnitude larger than any plausible plan-sale signal.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: 144 or Form 4 bodies showing off-plan sales by the CEO, CFO or a founder at a size comparable to a full session's volume.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The hunter says 'this is mostly priced' and it is right - every component is published, and published on the morning of the print in the same admissible sweep. The Needham target raise to $22.00 is a gurufocus news item captured at 15:08Z (docs/94ca8769ddaff2dce7685a3314d1bc4d7ac00ae3.txt, entries 2026-09-03T14:26:58Z and 14:26:28Z); the Estimize spread is a free public consensus page, the same source I judged as published for DOCU; and the 26% short-interest figure is itself in the captured stream at the 13:30:55Z entry. A broker target published hours before the release is the most visible form of expectation setting there is, and 'expectation stacking' is an interpretation of that published material, not a fact beyond it. The size is also small: $0.03 on EPS and $8.48m on revenue is well under one percent of a quarterly revenue base at this company's scale, and the 'institutional desks are monitoring this print with high intent' quote is unattributed promotional copy with no informational content. The one genuinely useful thing here is what the hunter flags itself: the 26% short interest points the other way, so the finding's own two halves cancel, which is why it declines to size it and why the band crosses zero.

Both findings lean on the same 30.1% run-up, #0 to argue insider selling is unpriced and #1 to argue expectations are stacked; those are the same bars read twice.
